interpretation.primary_unchanged: All15 source-mean lambda1 native sine/noise NMSE remains worse than lambda0. Median and deletion sensitivity do not replace the primary.
interpretation.sinusoid: syn:4942017 and syn:4942016 account for96.62% of positive paired NMSE deterioration. Their native response energy/history variance is3.54% and6.81% of the direction median (lowest2/15). Both also have genuine error-energy increases; not merely numerical-floor effects. Across all sources mean error/history variance decreases .00420398 to .00211081.
interpretation.noise: Electricity:T000129 and pedestrian:T000034 account for99.17% of positive paired NMSE deterioration. Electricity native energy/history variance is3.8616x median (rank13/15 ascending); error/history variance rises .0268935 to .1699058. Pedestrian rises .00207958 to .01345065. Actual adverse error increases drive this tail; all-source mean error/history variance rises .00742950 to .01462247.
interpretation.decomposition: Net source-mean NMSE worsening is86.61% orthogonal for sine and94.09% orthogonal for noise; this is an aggregate decomposition, not a universal per-source pattern. Electricity noise deterioration includes a large parallel component; pedestrian noise is predominantly orthogonal.
interpretation.influence: Predeclared removal of top1 or top2 paired deteriorations flips both directions to lower lambda1 means. These posthoc influence sensitivities retain the original primary and are not an exclusion rule.
interpretation.unit_weighting: Raw pooled energies and history-normalized pooled energies weight sources differently. Noise raw pooling improves .536958 to .274425 while normalized pooling worsens .513308 to1.010274; neither substitutes for source-average NMSE.
interpretation.hidden_output: Saved actual singleton hidden response NMSE improves for all15 sources in each direction, including adverse native-output cases. Correlations are descriptive; paired NMSE-change Spearman .110714 sine/.075 noise. No measured Jacobian or causal mechanism follows.
